freshness unknown never widens issuer authority

cases.name: freshness_risk_matrix
assertions: pending_local_only is never synchronized or federated

cases.name: global_decision_merge
assertions: an allow from one grant never short-circuits a stronger global outcome

cases.name: limited_timeline_state_at_window_start
cases.basis: confirmed RealmCommit prefix of the same stream up to the position preceding the window start
assertions: current state is never substituted for window-start state

cases.name: retry_after
cases.jitter_rule: add the injected 0..20 percent sample to local_backoff_delay only

cases.name: confusable_check
assertions: the SDK exposes this exact check as a callable utility
the single-input utility does not silently normalize before reporting
arkret_display_confusable_v1 validates both inputs before comparison
pairwise comparison uses the Unicode and UTS #39 versions pinned by string-profile-registry.json

cases.name: contact_petname_binding
assertions: the canonical input is RFC 8785 JCS for the two-element array
the server-visible suffix is exactly 43 unpadded base64url characters
the decrypted value carries peer.principal_id and is rejected on slot mismatch
petname is never auto-created from a profile display name
confirmed_display_name changes only on evidence-backed acceptance initialization or explicit identity confirmation
ordinary remark edits preserve confirmed_display_name and Realm or Directory names cannot initialize it

cases.name: invite_membership_transition_atomicity
assertions: ak.invite.create atomically writes invite_lifecycle and the invite_live_target slot while ak.invite.accept atomically writes invite_lifecycle, member_state join and the invite_live_target release
the membership FSM has no invite state and exact invite acceptance uses the registered leave to join edge
a rejected or revoked or expired invite changes only invite_lifecycle and leaves the member typed current result byte-identical
the 3PID create and revoke branches produce no member_state projection; claim produces only a subject-bound membership proposal
a direct member ban from leave is evaluated independently by the membership FSM
ak.invite.cancel is valid only for a stored direct invitee binding; token and 3PID invites require the high-risk ak.invite.revoke path
a direct cancel requires signed payload.invitee_account_id to equal the stored invitee binding
claimed to accepted is a registered invite FSM edge and ak.invite.accept must derive its from state from the frozen typed current result
a directed ak.invite.revoke to send_failed writes only invite_lifecycle and leaves the invite_live_target slot claimed
a third-party ak.invite.revoke writes only invite_lifecycle because its payload carries no invitee_account_id

the write count is branch-dependent, not per kind: ak.invite.accept and ak.invite.revoke derive the invite_live_target write only when the payload carries invitee_account_id, so a third-party accept is two writes and a send_failed or third-party revoke is one

cases.name: invite_live_target_uniqueness
assertions: the only source of truth for directed invite live uniqueness is invite_live_target whose subject is the single-component composite over canonical_json(payload.invitee_account_id) and never contains realm_id

ak.invite.create carries expected_revision null for that typed current result and the RealmCommit additionally derives the full head-identity guard for it; a second directed create for the same account is rejected with failed_precondition and invite_live_target_occupied, enters no canonical history and derives no typed current result write
the rejection details are closed to reason_code, invite_id and create_event_id and MUST NOT be reported as cas_conflict

two concurrent directed creates contend on the same typed current result so exactly one wins under the authority-commit basis and the loser is rejected, independent of any implementation-private index or insertion order

a terminal invite releases the slot with an explicit set null write that keeps its own head, and a later create for the same account is accepted; a create whose basis is pinned to an earlier free state is still rejected because the head identities differ even though both settle to null
reaching expires_at does not release the slot; only a registered Event does, so the slot stays claimed until ak.invite.revoke with target_state expired is accepted
send_failed keeps the slot claimed and the payload schema forbids invitee_account_id there, so the client must revoke before creating a replacement invite
a third-party invite whose revoke payload carries a forged invitee_account_id fails stored_field_matches_payload with reducer_projection_failed and releases no slot
a directed invite whose terminal revoke omits invitee_account_id fails the same predicate, so a directed invite cannot leak a permanently claimed slot
the slot value is the literal ak:event: create_event_id; a release Event whose expected_revision carries the ak:invite: spelling is failed_precondition

cases.name: join_policy_gate_axis_orthogonality
assertions: principal_admission and cooldown are evaluated under every default_join_rule including public, invite and closed
ak.invite.create fails before invite_lifecycle and ak.invite.accept fails before either invite_lifecycle or member_state when the hard gate rejects
closed blocks applicant-initiated entry only; the four authorized-writer branches stay available
the DM bootstrap batch reaches active member count 2
adding a third member to an active DM Realm is still rejected

cases.name: holder_quarantine_disclosure_indistinguishable
assertions: all five variants return a byte-identical response body and status code
timing difference across the equivalence class is at most 50ms
the response never carries disclosed_outcome=quarantined; that value is not in the enum
high trust introduction evidence does not widen disclosure, because the leak is consent state and not existence
invite delivery, contact delivery and ak.self.consent.command.request.v1 expose no observable that distinguishes quarantine from rejection
invite delivery and ak.self.consent.command.request.v1 each write one holder quarantine entry whose surface_kind is invite_delivery and consent_request respectively
contact delivery writes only the Contact pending_incoming head and never a holder quarantine entry, while still consuming one new-source quota slot
the consent_request branch carries no Event ref and none of introduction_kind, effective_kind, trust_tier, invite_event_id, request_digest or idempotency_key_digest; its consent_scope excludes invite
the invite_delivery branch keeps all six members required and pins consent_scope to invite; any cross-branch member is a schema violation
consent_request deduplicates by live-entry uniqueness over (account_id, source_peer_principal_id, consent_scope) because that operation has no idempotency key and no nonce

cases.name: invite_claim_expiry_canonical_time
assertions: expiry compares the signed claim event created_at against the invite expires_at and never uses receiver-local now
all clock variants and the backfill replay produce identical outcome and identical invite typed current result value
the rejected claim writes no shared effect
pending to expired must come from a separate accepted ak.invite.revoke Event

cases.name: device_pairing_challenge_transcript
assertions: the verifier independently rebuilds the complete challenge transcript before signature verification
new_device_pubkey canonical bytes and digest remain identical across stage, resolve and gate
stage accepts only the canonical PublicKey shape and rejects a target proof minted before server challenge material exists
the gate request requires one still-pending staged request and rejects every client-supplied substitute transcript
stage resolve and status remain account-less and expose neither principal binding nor sibling targets
an unauthorized fresh device receives no SessionGrant and cannot call any self device-messages operation
the gate request requires a ready_for_claim record and refuses one that is still staged

cases.name: device_pairing_accepted_device_attestation
assertions: the accepted_device possession object is closed over account_id, device_id, device_public_key_did, hpke_key, algorithms, device_key_algorithm, authorization_binding_kind and pairing_challenge_transcript_digest, and over nothing the approving device chooses
the approving device and the Account Authority each rebuild that object independently and never accept a requester-supplied attestation copy
pairing_challenge_transcript_digest is compared against a locally recomputed challenge transcript before signature verification
hpke_key and algorithms are read only from the verified attestation; neither the stage request nor the bootstrap carries them
the target attestation travels only in the out-of-band QR or short-link fragment and is never returned by stage or resolve
a transcript minted for one authorization_binding_kind never verifies for the other in either direction
the target device fetches the accepted authorize Event and verifies byte-identical device_signature, byte-identical key material and an expected principal_id before it assembles the identity locally
account_id is a signed member obtained from the candidate's own pending account handoff; a server side channel, a route, a session audience or an unsigned body member never substitutes for it
the authenticated finalize call is the only server-facing carrier of the proof, and the anonymous stage and resolve request surfaces still refuse it

cases.name: device_pairing_code_claim
assertions: the stage response and the stored record carry no principal and no AccountId, and the record state is staged
a pairing code is unique across the whole live pending set of the service, and a second stage call mints a distinct request and a distinct code

finalize recomputes the challenge transcript from the service's own durable stage, verifies the candidate signature with the staged new_device_pubkey, and requires target_proof.account_id to equal the AccountId the presented account handoff is bound to
finalize moves the record from staged to ready_for_claim one way; no run returns to staged and no run reaches authorized without passing through it

a successful finalize moves every other unaccepted ready_for_claim record of the same AccountId to terminal expired in the same durable transaction, so the account never holds two approvable records at once
the supersession key is the AccountId alone: reusing the candidate key (a refreshed pairing page) and minting a fresh candidate key (a different new device) retire the earlier record identically
a superseded record keeps a bounded tombstone that covers at least its own expires_at, so its code stays consumed for the rest of the window it could otherwise be replayed in
a record already accepted by pair_device keeps its terminal outcome: a later finalize for the same account never rewrites it and its exact replay still returns the same authorized_event_ref
an exact finalize retry returns the same outcome and performs no second supersession
the superseded request is not_found for code claim, resolve and pair_device, while status with the correct request id and pairing code reports expired, indistinguishable from a naturally elapsed TTL
an exact finalize retry returns the same outcome without re-attaching a proof, and the same request id with different canonical content conflicts
the code claim returns the same bootstrap and a byte-equivalent target proof as the QR and link path for the same request
the claim response carries no private key, no session credential, no recovery material and nothing about any other device of the account, and it grants no long-lived authority

an unknown, wrong, expired, superseded, cross-account, not yet finalized and already consumed code all return one indistinguishable not_found with no observable difference in body, code, reason code or timing
the pairing code never appears in a URL path or query string, an access log or an analytics event
exceeding the per-caller-device, per-AccountId or per-service rate budget returns rate_limited; those transport buckets neither replace nor reset the exact-request failure budget

the Account Authority verifies an active Standard human SessionGrant and exact HTTP DPoP JTI, applies all transport buckets, and obtains a fresh matching allow receipt through ak.peer.device_revocations.command.check.v1 with action_class device_pairing_code_claim before it performs any pairing-code lookup

the origin Station compares both expected selectors from the signed device_binding against its locked durable current projection; the SessionGrant snapshot alone never authorizes claim, and device_pairing_code_claim is never represented as event_write

revocation_pending, revoked, authority_mismatch, generation_mismatch, receipt mismatch or expiry, and origin unavailability all fail closed before pending lookup with no code-dependent disclosure and no request-id failure-budget write

after allow, only the Account Authority reads its single gate-side pending and abuse ledger; the origin current-device gate receives an intent digest rather than the plaintext pairing code and never reads or mirrors pairing state

only a failure after an exact retained request is located can create or increment the ledger row keyed by device_pairing_request_id; an unknown request id or a code that resolves to no exact request creates no row
the first nine counted failures leave staged or ready_for_claim unchanged, while the tenth count, pending-to-expired transition, code consumption and bounded tombstone are one durable transaction
a failed counter transaction rolls back both the increment and pending-state transition, so no partial abuse-control or business write is observable
byte-identical replay of a successful finalize or terminal pair_device result never counts, and authorized or durable pair_device terminal outcomes are never rewritten by later failures

counting or lockout never changes the existing not_found, proof_invalid or duplicate_conflict surface, reveals the count, authors an Event, grants authority, writes a typed current result or records a success outcome

cases.name: per_stream_window_start_basis
cases.basis: realm_sync_entry.streams[].window_start_basis, evaluated once per stream_ref and never inherited from a sibling stream of the same Realm bucket
assertions: one frame carries a mixed Realm, Circle and Sidecar window start and each stream states its own coverage
state_at_window_start is display context and MUST NOT clear any stream's preview_only
stream_genesis MUST NOT carry anchor_position or anchor_commit_ref; the other two anchor kinds MUST carry both
before_readable_floor accepts a non-zero oldest_position as the start of the permitted prefix and does not require position 0
a stream whose basis is insufficient MUST NOT enter reducer input or the MLS install path while its siblings continue

cases.name: stream_scan_permitted_range_paging
cases.basis: physical stream positions 0..12 with a caller permitted 4..9 through membership_join, limit 3
assertions: truncated reports only Commits the caller is permitted to read, so positions 10..12 MUST NOT set it
an empty commits[] with truncated false MUST NOT be read as an absent or empty physical stream
readable_floor.oldest_position is 4 and floor_commit_id is the Commit at 4, so the permitted prefix is verifiable without position 0
the commit at the floor is the only readable row allowed to carry an unresolvable previous_commit_ref
newer.previous_commit_ref equals older.commit_id in both directions and across the page boundary between the first and second page
a request carrying both or neither of after_position and before_position is a schema violation and MUST NOT be repaired by defaulting a direction
the scan surface MUST reject an ak:cursor: value and MUST NOT issue one

cases.name: stream_enumeration_has_no_starvation
cases.basis: one Realm with 70 streams visible to the caller, a 64-entry subscribe window and ak.self.realm.read.streams.v1 paging
assertions: a stream outside the first 64 MUST remain discoverable, readable and continuously updatable
the first 64 slots MUST NOT be permanently occupied by a fixed set, and the server MUST NOT silently drop a tail
pagination is one fixed generation: a stream appearing after page one is never inserted into an earlier page and therefore never skipped
discovery of an added or removed stream MUST NOT be suppressed by an event-kind filter
stream_refs entries MUST be unique, MUST name a Realm in realm_ids and MUST each be permitted; a non-permitted entry is rejected rather than dropped
enumeration order and subscribe truncation order are both unsigned bytes of JCS(stream_ref), so the two agree on which streams a bounded window kept

cases.name: event_read_row_integrity_and_existence_acl
cases.basis: stream_row pairs of one RealmCommit and the EventReadRow member in the same row
assertions: a mismatch between event_id and commit.event_ref MUST be rejected and MUST NOT be reconciled by preferring either side
commit.event_ref already names the source Event, so a stub in this position MUST carry event_id and the stub name is not a privacy guarantee
redacted and locked rows are not complete reducer input
existence ACL is enforced on the whole row, so the Commit MUST NOT be used to leak an Event the caller may not know exists

cases.name: zero_window_and_empty_stream
cases.basis: realm_stream_window scalars read against the caller's permitted range
assertions: a zero-row window MUST NOT be read as an empty or exhausted stream
complete proves delivery of the frozen window only, never that the stream was read down to position 0
limited marks history the caller may read, so unreadable history below the floor MUST NOT set it and MUST NOT clear it
byte budgets decide segmentation only and MUST NOT lower window_limit or flip limited inside one window
